mechanism: One 250us delayed recheck after the unsuccessful immediate retirement readiness check; all subsequent retries retain 5ms. Preserve original short-circuit service/Blink predicates, callback ownership, 5s deadline and collection. Default-off feature FlashwrightEarlyRetirementRecheck. At most one extra check per retirement relative to baseline, no busy spin.
policy: Same candidate binary off/on, existing physical renderer reuse, classic uncapped early-idle frames, lazy VAAPI, locator cache off. Original launch policy checked before private additions. Four-core quota, CPUs0–5,8GiB,swap0,Nice10. No Playwright arm.

scope.testBodies: Unchanged original setup body;240 tests per timed capture. The enlarged suite is diagnostic and does not replace the original nine acceptance scenarios.
scope.timing: Complete original watchdog-owned interval including fixture/runner/browser startup and natural observed drain; cgroup charged CPU and peak memory kept distinct.
scope.auditPolicy: Attribution off/on; candidate API diagnostics and worker controls audit on in both arms; all suite timings audit off.

attribution.question: Does the existing fixed5ms worker-service retirement poll contribute materially to observed context.close latency? Distinguish number of readiness checks, worker-wait interval and retired-document collection interval.
attribution.decisionRule: Consider a completion-wakeup or bounded early-recheck experiment only if delayed readiness polling is observed in both audited captures and its warm median interval is at least2ms. Otherwise preserve the negative attribution and investigate another phase.

diagnosticAdvancementRule: Both reversed 15-context comparisons reduce warm context-close median by at least 20%, preserve all outcomes and natural drain; audit must show earlier completed checks.

result.limitations: Public lifecycle outcomes and fresh successor state; does not force native registry/event race order or prove every worker shutdown path.

workerInterpretation: Both arms pass acknowledged dedicated/nested/shared/service-worker execution, immediate construction and explicit termination, followed by fresh successor storage/cache/registration/global state. Busy infinite-loop worker retirement takes about2s in both arms; enabled service case needs a third check. All14 retirements transfer per arm. These observations preserve slow-path waiting but do not force every native race.
suiteAdvancementRule: If diagnostics and worker lifecycle controls pass, run unchanged setup body at 15-test preflight and 240-test timing, workers1/4, two reversed blocks, audit off in timed suite. Advance to original applications only if complete elapsed improves at least10% in both worker counts and both orders without >5% charged CPU regression.

decision.reason: Single-worker waiting and four-worker CPU contention limit different portions of complete work; the measurements do not establish a universal causal CPU bound.

limitations: Two reversed blocks, no confidence interval, no application expansion or final acceptance.
One fast retry shifts later nominal checks from5,10ms to5.25,10.25ms and can slightly delay a slower teardown. Readiness still precedes deadline evaluation, as in the baseline.
Warm diagnostic medians exclude the first context. Native completion logs perturb the diagnostic and are not a CPU/removable-work bound.
Native worker registry/event races, held script response startup, duplicate closure and browser-close races were not added to this screen. No new native unit cases were run.
A successful fresh successor and absence of observed survivors do not establish exhaustive callback/resource custody or public release readiness.
